analytic.title: Real-Time Execution based on Fluid Scheduling by using IPC Control Scheme

div.p: Fluid scheduling is an optimal real-time scheduling applicable to multiprocessor systems and is a scheduling model so that every real-time task is executed at a constant speed from release time to deadline. It is necessary for fluid scheduling to control the execution speed of each task. But, since the execution speed of the task is invariable in a conventional general purpose processor. Therefore, fluid scheduling is conventionally achieved by repeatedly executing and stopping tasks. However, this method incurs significant overheads due to frequent task switching. On the other hand, fluid scheduling without overhead by using an IPC control scheme has been proposed. The IPC control scheme controls the execution speed of each thread in an SMT processor. We propose a new IPC control scheme to extract thread-level parallelism and improve throughput effectively, also improving the schedulability of the fluid schedule. The evaluation results show that the proposed method improved the total throughput of the fluid schedule.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: In a real-time system, the value of a process depends not only on its result but also on its completion time, and the system works appropriately by executing tasks while meeting their time constraints. This research targets hard real-time systems like an autonomous car, which require high-precision real-time processing. Real-time scheduling guarantees the time constraints of all real-time tasks in a real-time system, determining the order of task execution by obtaining task priority from their time constraints. Fluid scheduling is an optimal realtime scheduling applicable to multiprocessor systems and is a scheduling model so that every real-time task is executed at a constant speed from release time to deadline. A generalpurpose processor can't control execution speed, so fluid scheduling is conventionally emulated by repeatedly executing and stopping tasks [1]. However, this method has a significant context switching overhead.

By contrast, a method for fluid scheduling without overhead has been proposed using an IPC (Instruction Per Clock cycle) control scheme controlling the execution speed of each thread in an SMT (Simultaneous Multithreaded) processor [2]. Based on the target IPC and the control period set by software, the IPC control scheme controls the thread execution speed, observing the number of instructions committed per control period, regulating the IPC by changing the number of instructions to be fetched in each period. The conventional IPC control scheme stops instruction fetch when the number of commited instructions during control period exceeds a certain threshold. This scheme stops instruction fetch from the threads with the lower target IPC in order, so that there is a section where a few threads with the higher target IPC only execute. This scheme cannot fully extract the TLP (Thread Level Parallelism).

To sufficiently extract the TLP, we propose a new IPC control scheme for fluid scheduling in SMT processors, called Variable Frequency IPC Control (VF-IPC). VF-IPC controls the frequency of instruction fetches of each thread according to the target IPC. It controls the fetchable interval based on the target IPC and the number of instructions committed during the control period. Each thread fetches instructions at a fixed frequency so that a thread with a high target IPC does not execute alone in the latter half of the control period. In this way, the number of intervals in which multiple threads execute simultaneously increases, and the total throughput is improved by using TLP. jhe VF-IPC control scheme can also improve the schedulability of fluid scheduling.

The evaluation results show that the VF-IPC effectively extracts TLP and improves the total throughput, and improves the schedulability of fluid scheduling over the conventional scheme. The rest of this paper is organized as follows: in section 2, we describe background work; in section 3, we introduce related studies; in section 4, we propose VF-IPC; in section 5, we describe the evaluation environment and results; Finally, in section 6, we conclude this study.

div.head: A. Fluid scheduling
div.p: Fluid schedule is an optimal real-time scheduling that can be applied to multiprocessor systems, executing tasks at a constant speed from release time to deadline. The solid red line in Fig. 1 represents the ideal execution according to a fluid schedule. Here, the horizontal axis represents time, the vertical axis represents the remaining execution time, and the scale of each axis is equal. The up arrow represents the release time of a task, and the down arrow represents the deadline of the task. We can see that task is executed at a constant speed.

div.head: B. SMT Processor
div.p: In an SMT processors, multiple threads execute in parallel while sharing hardware resources such as instruction pipelines, functional units, cache systems, etc. This technique improves the total throughput of the entire system in exchange for the throughput per single thread because it takes advantage of TLP and can hide various latencies such as cache misses and branch prediction misses. However, the most SMT processors suffer from resource conflict among threads, making it difficult to predict the execution time of the tasks when used in real-time systems [3].

div.head: C. IPC Control Scheme
div.p: In order to improve the predictability of execution time in SMT processors, an IPC control scheme has been proposed to control the execution speed of each thread [4] [2] [5]. Based on the target IPC and the control period set by software, the IPC control scheme observes the number of instructions committed per control period, and controls the IPC by changing the number of instructions to be fetched per control period.

div.head: D. PID Control
div.p: The PID control is one of the most popular feedback control methods that absorbs the effects of external disturbances and brings the output closer to the target value [6]. Assuming that the proportional gain is Kp, the integral gain is Ki, the derivative gain is Kd, and the error is e(t), the PID control can be expressed by Equation ( 1) and (2).
div.formula: output = K P e(t) + K I t 0 e(t)dt + K D d dt e(t)(1)
div.p: E. RT-DVFS with Fluid schedule using IPC control scheme DVFS (Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling) is one of the methods to reduce power consumption, which achieves a trade-off between power consumption and performance by varying the operating voltage and frequency. In addition, RT-DVFS (Real-Time DVFS) has been proposed to perform DVFS while guaranteeing the time constraint in real-time systems. In SMT processor, RT-DVFS requires complex processing to guarantee real-time performance, because the operating frequency variation affects the execution speed of all threads. By controlling the execution speed of each thread using the IPC control scheme based on fluid scheduling, RT-DVFS can be realized with little overhead.

div.head: A. Pseudo-Fluid Scheduling
div.p: A conventional general purpose processor cannot execute the tasks according to the slope of a fluid schedule because the execution speed of tasks cannot be changed and controlled dynamically. P-Fair (Proportionate Fair) scheduling has been proposed so as to execute all jobs along to the fluid schedule by repeatedly executing and stopping the tasks at every tick [1]. The P-Fair scheduling has been proven to be optimal. In Fig. 1, the remaining execution time decreases by the time the task is executed, so task execution is represented as a line with a slope of 45 , and the time without task execution is represented as a line with a slope of 0 . The execution of a task is represented by a solid black line in Fig. 1 when the task is repeatedly executed and stopped according to the P-Fair. Since P-Fair switches tasks at every scheduler tick, context switches occur frequently, and the overhead becomes very large. DP-Fair, an improved version of P-Fair scheduling, has been proposed to reduce context switch overhead [7]. However, the overhead is still significant because the essence of repeatedly executing and stopping tasks remains unchanged [8].

div.head: B. Fluid Scheduling by Using IPC Control Scheme
div.p: An IPC control scheme that controls the execution speed of each thread to achieve fluid scheduling without overhead has been proposed [9]. This scheme executes a task at a constant speed from release time to deadline by setting the target IPC based on the slope of the fluid schedule. DFS (Dynamic Frequency Scaling) is another method to change the execution speed of tasks, but it is not suitable to achieve a fluid schedule because the change in frequency affects the execution speed of all threads in SMT processors.

div.head: C. IPC Control Scheme
div.p: The conventional IPC control scheme controls the IPC of each task by stopping instruction fetch when the number of committed instructions in a control period exceeds an upper limit. The IPC control scheme is illustrated in Fig. 2. The upper limit is calculated from the number of instructions committed per control period and the target IPC. When the number of instructions committed per control period exceeds the upper limit, the IPC control unit stops fetches from the thread. This control scheme has a disadvantage that TLP cannot be extracted sufficiently. Fig. 3 shows four real-time threads executing in parallel, ordered by decreasing target IPC. At the beginning of the control period, four threads are executing simultaneously. However, the number of committed instructions reaches the upper limit starting from thread 4 with the lowest target IPC and its instruction fetch stops. Finally, the thread1 that has the highest target IPC executes alone. Since TLP cannot be utilized in the section where the thread is executing alone, it is clear that the conventional IPC control scheme has room for improvement in throughput.

div.head: IV. VF-IPC
div.p: The conventional IPC control scheme has a problem on extracting TLP due to the existence of sections where threads execute alone. To address this issue, we propose the Variable Frequency IPC control scheme (VF-IPC) that controls the frequency of fetching of each thread according to the target IPC. This scheme takes the target IPC and the number of instructions committed during the control period as input and performs feedback control using the fetchable interval I as output. In this scheme, each thread fetches instructions at a fixed frequency during the control period so that a thread with a high target IPC does not execute alone in the latter half of the control period. In this way, the section where multiple threads execute simultaneously becomes long, so that the total throughput improves. The proposed IPC control scheme can also improve the schedulability of fluid scheduling.

div.head: A. Design of VF-IPC
div.p: In order to control the frequency of fetching according to the target IPC, the fetchable interval I shall be controlled. 4 shows four real-time threads executing in parallel, ordered by decreasing target IPC. If an instruction is fetched from the target thread, the instruction fetch from the thread stops at next clock, and the instruction fetch from the thread is enabled after the I interval. In this sheme, each thread fetches instructions at a constant frequency during the control period. The section in which multiple threads execute in parallel becomes long with respect to the conventional scheme, and more TLP can be extracted to improve throughput. Conflicts among threads and various latencies caused by cache misses and branch prediction misses are dealt by feeding back the number of instructions committed in the control period and updating the interval I.

div.head: V. EVALUATION A. Target Processor
div.p: The VF-IPC is implemented in Responsive Multi-threaded Processor Unit (RMT PU), which is an 8-way prioritized SMT processor, as shown in Fig. 6 in SRMTP SoC designed for distributed real-time control, especially for spacecraft systems systems [10]. The RMTPU can execute up to eight realtime threads simultaneously by controlling the computational resources allocated to each thread based on priority. In our evaluation, we make the priorities of all threads equal, similar to a general SMT processor. The detailed parameters of the RMT PU are shown in Table I. The VF-IPC control scheme is designed and implemented inside the IPC control unit of the RMT PU (CPU front-end in Fig. 6) by Verilog HDL. We evaluate the VF-IPC by simulation using Cadence XCELIUM Parallel Simulator.

div.head: B. Accuracy Evaluation
div.p: To evaluate whether the VF-IPC control scheme can adequately control IPC by varying the frequency of fetches, we evaluated the accuracy of IPC control. We use the error rate (errorRate) of IPC control as an evaluation indicator of accuracy. The errorRate is defined by Equation 5 using the target IPC (IP C target )and the IPC at runtime (IP C actual ).
div.formula: errorRate = |IP C aucual -IP C target | IP C target (5)
div.p: Although the error tolerance varies from application to application, considered an error rate of 5% or less acceptable for this evaluation. Benchmark programs including bitcnt, strsearch, patricia, and ADPCM.enc from the Mibench embedded benchmark suite [11] are selected and used for evaluation. The measured IPC, branch prediction miss rate, and cache miss rate for single-threaded execution of each benchmark program is shown in Table II. Three workloads shown in Table III were used for evaluation. Workload 1 consists of four benchmarks. Workload 2 consists only of ADPCM.enc, with a high cache miss rate and branch prediction miss rate. Workload 3 consists only of strsearch, with a low cache miss rate, low branch prediction miss rate, and high IPC. We used ipcRate, the ratio of the target IPC (IP C target ) to the IPC during single-threaded execution (IP C single ), as a parameter for evaluation. ipcRate is defined by Equation 6. The evaluation results for each workload are shown in Fig. 7, 8, 9. Fig. 7 shows that for workload 1, the VF-IPC control scheme was able to control up to 80% of ipcRate, while the conventional scheme controlled up to 70%. This result shows that the VF-IPC control scheme has improved the accuracy of control. From Fig. 8, we can see that both methods can control up to 80% ipcRate for workload 2. When the ipcRate is less than 80%, the VF-IPC control scheme has better control accuracy than the conventional scheme. The accuracy of the VF-IPC control scheme dropped drastically at 90% because there is only one memory access unit and the memory access becomes a bottleneck. These results imply that the VF-IPC control scheme can effectively deal with branch prediction errors by extracting TLP. Fig. 9 shows that both methods can control up to 50% for workload 3. This evaluation shows that the VF-IPC control scheme can control workloads with low cache miss rate and branch prediction miss rate with the same accuracy as the conventional method. For both the conventional IPC control scheme and VF-IPC control scheme, we selected the PID control parameters Kp, Ki, and Kd among five: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.97, and picked the one with the highest accuracy from 125 combinations.
div.formula: ipcRate = IP C target /IP C single (6)

div.head: C. Throughput Evaluation
div.p: To find out if VF-IPC improves the throughput of IPC control, we evaluated the upper limit of the total IPC that all tasks can control without missing the deadline. As the ipcRate of all threads running is set in increments of 10% in the range of 10%-100%, we evaluated the upper limit of the total IPC that all tasks can control without missing the deadline. Fig. 10 shows that VF-IPC improves the throughput by 44% on average and up to 75% compared to the conventional methods. Since the throughput can be improved most effectively in workload2 where the branch prediction miss is the highest, this result shows that VF-IPC can effectively extract TLPs and execute tasks without deadline-missing based on the Fluid schedule even when the total throughput is high.

div.head: D. Synthesis Evaluation
div.p: We synthesized baseline RMTPU with the conventional IPC control, IPC control module, and fetch thread selectors. We performed synthesis with Synopsys Design Compiler 2018.06-SP3 and used TSMC 130 nm process library for synthesis. We evaluated the hardware cost of VF-IPC for the ratio of the standard cell area of RMTP. As the Table IV shows, the area overhead of VF-IPC is minimal compared to the whole CPU frontend and RMTPU. Using an IPC control scheme that controls the execution speed of each thread in an SMT processor, fluid scheduling can be performed without incurring context switch overhead. However, the conventional IPC control scheme stops the instruction fetching of the target thread when the number of commits in the control period exceeds the upper limit. So there is room for improvement in TLP extraction because there is a section where the thread with highest target IPC executes alone.

We proposed the VF-IPC control scheme, which controls the frequency of instruction fetching according to the target IPC. The VF-IPC control scheme effectively extracts TLP by increasing the number of sections where multiple threads execute in parallel. The results of the throughput evaluation show that the VF-IPC control scheme improves the throughput by 44% on average and up to 75% compared to the conventional methods.
As future work, we will extend the VF-IPC control scheme to support RT-DVFS and achieve very low overhead RT-DVFS in an SMT processor.
